title: SVX2 FastROM Video Proof
desc: A real NASA camera frame compressed with SVX2, staged and decoded on the 65816, then displayed through Mode 7. The measured FastROM pipeline reaches 60.5–64.7 fps; this compact proof ROM holds one byte-verified frame.
keys: Self-running — decodes and displays the verified Artemis launch frame
pageDesc: Run a real SNES FastROM that decodes an SVX2-compressed NASA Artemis camera frame on the 65816 and displays it through Mode 7.
heading: SVX2 FastROM Video Proof
lede: A real NASA Artemis launch camera frame, compressed as SVX2, decoded by hand-tuned 65816 assembly, and displayed through Mode 7 in a genuine 32 KiB FastROM cartridge image.
keysHtml: Self-running — the ROM decodes, verifies, and holds the Artemis launch frame.
doc:
What this proves

The cartridge performs the real ROM-segment staging DMA, decodes a representative SVX2 delta packet, compares all 4,480 output bytes with the host oracle, uploads the result to Mode 7 character VRAM, and only then releases force blank.

60 fps result

The separate VBlank-counted target gate charges staging, assembly decode, and the 4,480-byte presentation DMA. With FastROM enabled correctly in the cartridge header, MEMSEL, and execution bank, the representative median and worst-size packets reach 60.5 and 64.7 fps. This gallery cartridge intentionally holds one verified frame; the full moving reel and functional high-WRAM refill loop remain the next integration step.

Source footage: NASA Artemis I press-site camera, November 16, 2022. Hit Verify fidelity to reproduce the ROM's WRAM success gate live in this tab.
